## Statute
§1(c) - Tax for unmarried individuals
§63(c) - Itemized deductions
§151(d)(1) - Exemption amount of $2,000

## Reasoning
Alice is an unmarried individual (she paid Bob for work, not a marital relationship), so §1(c) applies.

Gross income: $133,200
Itemized deductions: $2,939 + $8,744 = $11,683
Personal exemption (single, no dependents): $2,000

Taxable income = $133,200 - $11,683 - $2,000 = $119,517

Since $119,517 is over $115,000 but not over $250,000, under §1(c)(iv):
Tax = $31,172 + 36% × ($119,517 - $115,000)
Tax = $31,172 + 36% × $4,517
Tax = $31,172 + $1,626.12
Tax = $32,798.12

Rounded to whole number: $32,798

## Answer
Answer: 32798

## Statute
§1(c) - Tax for unmarried individuals
§63(d) - Itemized deductions
§151(d)(1) - Exemption amount of $2,000
§3301 - Excise tax on employers (FUTA)
§3306(a)(1) - Definition of employer

## Reasoning
Alice is an unmarried individual (she paid Bob for work, not a marital relationship), so §1(c) applies.

**Income Tax Calculation:**
Gross income: $133,200
Itemized deductions (per §63(d)): $2,939 + $8,744 = $11,683
Personal exemption (per §151(d)(1)): $2,000

Taxable income = $133,200 - $11,683 - $2,000 = $119,517

Since $119,517 is over $115,000 but not over $250,000, under §1(c)(iv):
Income tax = $31,172 + 36% × ($119,517 - $115,000)
Income tax = $31,172 + 36% × $4,517
Income tax = $31,172 + $1,626.12 = $32,798.12

**FUTA Tax Calculation:**
Alice paid Bob $4,512 for work. Under §3306(a)(1), Alice is an employer (wages > $1,500).
Under §3301, FUTA tax = 6% of total wages.
FUTA tax = 6% × $4,512 = $270.72

**Total Tax:**
$32,798 (income tax, rounded) + $271 (FUTA tax, rounded) = $33,069
